newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend loss, seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend loss, seen falling.

text.p: Polish shares fell for the second straight day on Thursday and analysts saw them entering a more significant downtrend as many stocks were overvalued after the bourse gained about 38 percent in the last two months.
Some analysts said they expected a flat market on Friday while others saw it rising and possibly setting 35-month highs on Friday and early next week, before a correction hits.

The main market's WIG index fell 88.4 points, or 0.5 percent, to 18,206.6, and turnover fell 25.7 percent to 250.8 million zlotys ($83.3 million) on both markets as 38 issues fell, 28 rose and 22 were flat.

"All ratios of technical analysis are overheated and show sell-signals, companies earnings reports for January were not spectacular, so surely the correction will happen," said Pawel Dmytryk, an analyst at Bank Staropolski brokerage.
Some analysts said the expected profit-taking correction could last about a month and was likely to pull the WIG index down to 16,000 points.

They said, however, Poland's good economic prospects and expanding possibilities such as new issues and forthcoming large privatisations were attracting new, foreign capital, which could later push the WIG index up.

The third floor of the bourse - the free market for small and less liquid stocks -- had its first stock listed on Thursday when garment maker Elpo SA started trade at 30 zlotys ($10), 36.4 percent higher than its issue price.
Computer maker Optimus SA jumped 5.8 percent after Wednesday's 10-percent plunge, helped by the company's forecast of 1997 net profit rising 80 percent, traders said.
Continuous trade turnover amounted to 19.3 million zlotys ($6.4 million) with the WIG 20 index closing at 1,864.7 points, 0.4 percent lower than in the regular session.
